## 6. A companion result: when the physical bath contains the complete complement

A separate construction addresses another access obstacle: an initially mixed bath whose purifier is unavailable.

It gives a broad operational principle, with a precise restriction.

Let \(\mathcal N\) be an **extreme CPTP channel**, with minimal complementary channel \(\mathcal C\) of output dimension \(r\). Suppose it is physically implemented by an isometry acting on the source and an initially uncorrelated mixed bath state \(\tau\). Let \(\mathcal B\) be the channel to the **whole physical outgoing bath**.

Then

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal B(\rho)
=
W\bigl[\mathcal C(\rho)\otimes\tau\bigr]W^\dagger
}

for an isometry \(W\).

Therefore the physical bath and the complete minimal complement are reversibly equivalent under local CPTP output processing. Access to the initial bath’s external purifier is unnecessary.
